doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Richmond family, gospel father and hearing Charlie Parker
summary: Smith's family was musical, his father sang in the Harmonizing Four; hearing Parker play with strings made him want to play jazz, then Morgan State.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: It’s a bit of a miracle I guess. You attended music college. I wonder if you had intentions to be a music teacher?

No, but I’m glad — I went to, when I finished high school, Armstrong High School in Richmond, Virginia, because my whole family was always music. And my father was in a harmonizing Gospel group, the Harmonizing Four Gospel group. And so I was just surrounded by music from day one and then actually you said earlier, you’ve got that poster by you of Charlie Parker. I was in high school when I heard Charlie Parker play “Just Friends” with strings over at someone’s house. That’s when I said well what is he doing? They say — because it was so beautiful. They say he’s playing jazz and doing improvisation. I said oh man, that’s what I want to do. So when I left Richmond I thought I was going to New York but, I’m glad I did go to Morgan State University which was in Baltimore.
